title: GS21 RECALIBRATED to a larger investment option (imax 500) with the priced y factor on the INVESTMENT COST, three exposure types
question: Does a priced second factor make a fair gap in GS21 when firm exposure runs through the investment option, as KP14's does through its growth options?
notes:
WHY (2026-10-10). At the Table I calibration the investment option is a modest, leverage-like share of GS21 equity (16-34%), and five y-factor constructions left the premium linear in the ranks with the market spanning 69-94% of SR_max. KP14's gap is a rank-nonlinearity of the growth-option share, so this spec first RECALIBRATES GS21 to a larger option -- the investment-cost ceiling imax 2000 -> 500, which quadruples the option's share of equity (optshare.py on low-res solves: mean 0.18 -> 0.75 by the crude per-period-surplus capitalisation) while the solve still converges (imax 200 and 100 make the firm's value explode: the option is then cheaper than the growth it buys) -- and then puts the priced y factor on the investment cost with three exposure types, exp(gs_bi y), gs_bi <= 0. Everything else is gvy25's (9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35). No level compensation.

CALIBRATION (low resolution, xnum 41, znum 50, bnum 10, NY 9, 150 firms, 2026-10-10 14:00). imax 500 with gs_bi 0 / -0.25 / -0.5: type premia 1.5 / 5.6 / 6.7 %/yr, SR_max 0.26 / 0.33 / 0.48 by y-tercile, mean log size 7.60 / 6.13 / 6.14 -- the unexposed type invests most and is the largest, so the footprint is large and NON-monotone in exposure. gs_bi -1.0 pushes the high-y-tercile SR_max to 0.62 with a 9.6% top premium; the shallower ladder is used. The baseline premium at imax 500 is 1.5 %/yr (3.2 at imax 2000): a larger option lowers the equity premium.

CHECKS. E[M R] = 1 to 1e-15 on the calibration economies; imax enters the solve stage params and the simulator reads it from the solution. gs_bi = 0 and imax 2000 reproduce gvy25's solver.

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; ids read from the Quest solve logs by verify_gs_vy_klc.sh before any seed runs. NOTE this economy is OFF Table I (imax); it is a mechanism probe, not a calibrated GS21.

PREDICTION (2026-10-10, before the run). Market share of SR_max 60-85%; room +0.01 to +0.05; the decisive read is room_s against room. The premium dispersion is strongly y-dependent at low resolution (cs-sd of mu 0.0015 at low y vs 0.0033 at high y), the state-rotation pattern, so the risk is room without room_s. FALSIFIED as 'a larger option lets the KP mechanism port to GS21' if room_s is below +0.02 at the oracle stage or the fair gap is below +0.005.

changes: gs_bi [0.0, -0.25, -0.5]: each type's drawn investment cost x exp(gs_bi y); production and cost exposures 0
the y factor moves the COST, exp(gs_bc y), with types gs_bc [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]; production exposure gs_bv 0, no level compensation (at y = 0 every type pays the same cost)
everything else gvy25's: 9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).
